Let a = P(0). For an integer polynomial, P(x) − P(y) is divisible by x − y, which gives:

- a ≡ P(−10) = 145 ≡ 5 (mod 10)
- a ≡ P(9) = 164 ≡ 2 (mod 9)

By the Chinese Remainder Theorem, a ≡ 65 (mod 90), so a = 65 + 90k.

These conditions are also sufficient. Write P in Newton form on the nodes −10, 0, 9:

P(x) = 145 + c₁(x+10) + c₂x(x+10) + x(x+10)(x−9)Q(x),

where Q has integer coefficients. Then c₁ = (a−145)/10 must be an integer, and so must c₂ = ((164−a)/9 − c₁)/19.

With a = 65 + 90k:
- c₁ = 9k − 8
- (164 − a)/9 = 11 − 10k
- c₂ = (11 − 10k − 9k + 8)/19 = (19 − 19k)/19 = 1 − k

Both are integers for every k, so every a ≡ 65 (mod 90) is attainable.

The values of |a| are 65, 25 (at k = −1), 115, and so on, so the minimum is 25.

ANSWER: 25
